items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: and then I made some gigs with Mary Lou Williams, who you just mentioned. Used to rehearse with her with Julius Watkins.

ctx.x: A.T. was there. And when his mother would go to work, we’d go to his house and practice for these gigs. We had these twelve dollar, ten dollar dance gigs around up in Harlem and a place down in Midtown, the name will come to me. Where they used to have, City Center, they used to have some dances in there. Those were the gigs I could take, and Miles gave me a gig and Birdland, I think it was January 1950, with Miles, Fats, Navarro, Bud Powell, Buhaina, Art Blakey and myself, sometimes we were in there a few weeks…

I was like I was in heaven, every night I was there way ahead of time practicing, and these guys were big time stars, they’d come lolly-gagging, they’d come in, relax about two minutes before time they’d hit and I’d say, “Where are they, what’s wrong with…?” Boy, I was in heaven. Anyhow, that was some of the early gigs, and then I made some gigs with Mary Lou Williams, who you just mentioned. Used to rehearse with her with Julius Watkins.

items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: So I called in Percy Heath, for bass, a terrific bass player also.

ctx.x: But you just can't shift from the East Side -

Well, you can, but you can't shift overnight; you have to rehearse with them. We went in there and started blowing. Oscar was great to play with because we composed at least 3 tunes a night or more. He'd start a bass figure and I would play, and that is really my schtick, my whole way of doing. I like to compose while I'm playing.
